Close the tab you just typed in and never return to it again lest you want to fuck up your computer.

Welcome! I'm curious how software engineers handle fatigue from being on a monitor all day? Are you able to work in other locations or do you spend a majority of your time coding in one spot?

Well first of all use f.lux, I think that's helped me quite a bit.

Don't have light coming in front of you, avoid glare, and avoid side light in your peripheral vision. Take frequent breaks.

So in my early 20s, I used to have three monitors, one of which was pretty large (around 32"), and the other two were vertically mounted next to it.

I used to get migraines every other day. I dropped one of the monitor when my migraines started turning into mini-seizures and that helped immediately.

Long story short, I now just have the one monitor and remote desktop then alt+tab into my other machines. I'm less productive that way but headaches were debilitating after a while so overall productivity is up.

Also, I actually split the day into two 7 hour work days, then take a nap in the middle.

Sorry if that doesn't help very much.
Oh and for the second half I do 80% of my coding from my desktop, and 20% by remoting in from my laptop. It helps.
